newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Resources seen as the hottest new deal.
newsitem.headline: China Resources seen as the hottest new deal.

text.p: Hong Kong is poised for a slew of IPOs over the next few weeks and analysts say the one to watch is China Resources Beijing Land Ltd.
Beijing Land is the property arm of mainland trader, China Resources Enterprise Ltd.
The subscription period for its 300 million share offering is expected to open in the week ahead and the price range is put at HK$1.99 to HK$2.36 per share.
"Strong subscriptions are expected for Beijing Land," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities. He said the stock's China link was likely to be a strong attraction.

Beijing Land indirectly controls Beijing Huayuan Property Co Ltd, a development company which specialises in renovating and reconstructing old and dilapidated buildings in the Xicheng District of Beijing and developing large residential complexes around Beijing.
Anglo Chinese Corp Finance Ltd is joint lead manager and lead underwriter of the issue.
Pacific Concord Holding Ltd is also expected to offer 300 million shares of its Concord Land Development Co Ltd unit. The price range is set at HK$3.34 and HK$3.96 per share.
But analysts said the issue would lack the red-chip appeal that Beijing Land enjoys. Red-chips are Hong Kong incorporated and managed companies with considerable interests in China.

Concord Land is a property development and investment company which focuses primarily on the development of shopping malls and commercial complexes in major cities in China. Analysts said the stock was more associated with the China consumer market than the property market.
Concord Land also lacks red-chip appeal because its parent, Pacific Concord, is not a red-chip company.
"Even though they are both property concerns, Beijing Land and Concord Land have two different concepts," said Percy Au-Young, director of research of DBS Securities H.K. Ltd.
He added that Beijing Land was likely to get a stronger response.

"Beijing Land is expected to be more attractive because of its quality property portfolio," Kwong said. "It covers prime locations in Beijing, where we see no problems of oversupply of (residential and commercial units)."
The heavy flow of Hong Kong IPOs has raised demand for Hong Kong dollars of late and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) last week injected money into the interbank market due to tight liquidity.

SmarTone Telecommunications Holdings Ltd closed a global offering of 84 million shares on Friday and Arts Optical International Holdings Ltd and Anhui Expressway Co Ltd are expected to launch offerings in Hong Kong shortly.
SmarTone shares, offered at HK$21.25 per share subject to adjustment, are expected to begin trading on October 31.
Arts Optical, an eyeglass frame manufacturer, is expected to begin its IPO on Tuesday and raise about HK$85 million. Dealing in its shares is expected to commence on November 8.
China toll roads operator Anhui Expressway Co Ltd is also expected to launch a 493 million H-share offering next week at between HK$1.59 and HK$1.92 per share.
H shares are Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong.
Dealing in the shares is expected to begin on November 13.
Trading in Beijing Land shares is expected to begin on November 8 and Concord Land on November 7.
